title: What is live today
content:
# What is live today

EdgeSwarm is a centralized verifiable-work prototype, not a decentralized production network. The deployed Next.js app creates bounded uppercase-text jobs, signs worker results, replays the built-in computation, signs verifier decisions and records simulated credits.

A separate verified-job payment step prepares a wallet-approved 0.001 Solana Devnet SOL transfer with a job-bound Memo. The server checks the actual transaction before storing its receipt. This is not escrow or USDC settlement.

## Start here

- [Open the live mobile app](https://edge-swarm.vercel.app/)
- [Open the desktop dashboard](https://edge-swarm.vercel.app/dashboard)
- [Read the source repository](https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/EdgeSwarm)
- [Inspect the real payment evidence](https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/EdgeSwarm/blob/main/docs/evidence/devnet-payment.json)

## Evidence and limits

The current suite has 72 automated tests, including eight landing/documentation regression checks. CI builds the web app and an Android debug APK. One approved disposable-wallet transfer passed the live API flow and is inspectable on Solana Explorer. Those facts are not a security certification, independent verifier deployment, hardware attestation, zk proof or Mainnet readiness claim.

## Blueprint archive

The separate archive preserves the uploaded 100-page design. It is unvalidated proposed architecture. Its APIs, USDC assumptions, real-device claims and independent-worker descriptions must not be treated as current implementation documentation. Use the guides in this section to run the actual repository.

title: Run the actual repository
content:
# Run the actual repository

## Local setup

Use Node.js 22 and npm. The repository does not publish an @edgeswarm/sdk package.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/EdgeSwarm.git
cd EdgeSwarm
npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
npm test
npm run build
npm start -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3100
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:3100. Local development uses the in-memory session store when DATABASE_URL is absent. Each guest session expires after 30 minutes. Node.js 24 may also meet the declared engines range; CI targets Node.js 22.

## Check the API

In another terminal:

```sh
node scripts/smoke.mjs
```

The smoke harness creates isolated guest sessions and exercises real signing, simulated settlement, rejection, origin enforcement and headers. It sends no blockchain funds.

## Development server

```sh
npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3100
```

For serverless hosting, configure PostgreSQL as described in the deployment guide. Never put DATABASE_URL in a public client environment variable or commit an environment file.

title: Jobs API: runnable browser example
Roles and trust boundaries
content:
# Roles and trust boundaries

## One backend, different keys

The current worker and verifier run inside the same Next.js backend. They use different Ed25519 keys in the session engine. That role separation does not create independent operators or hardware isolation.

The engine signs a result envelope, checks assignment, job ID, nonce, expiry, policy, task, reward, identity, signature, integrity and deterministic replay, then signs a verdict. The settlement gate rechecks the evidence.

## Storage

Local mode uses a capped in-memory store. Vercel uses PostgreSQL-backed session snapshots with optimistic revision checks. Signing keys are serialized inside those backend snapshots; the database is part of the trusted computing base. Public receipt exports omit private keys.

## Not implemented

An independently deployed ProofAgent, real Android task execution in the web pipeline, GossipMarket peer discovery, on-chain escrow, USDC settlement, TEE attestation and zk verification are not established guarantees. The imported blueprint describes possible future architecture, not those features being available today.

title: Verified-job Devnet payment contract
content:
# Verified-job Solana Devnet payment contract

## Implemented sequence

1. A session-scoped job passes the core engine’s signed-evidence and replay gate.
2. `POST /api/jobs/:id/solana` with `{action:"prepare",payer,recipient}` fixes the payer, recipient and 1,000,000 lamport payment. Both addresses must be on-curve wallet keys and must differ.
3. The intent binds the job ID, task/result digests, signed verdict, worker/verifier identities, payer, recipient, amount, cluster, unique intent ID and validity window. The backend verifier signs its authorization. The Memo carries job ID, intent ID and the binding digest.
4. The server verifies the public RPC’s Devnet genesis hash and prepares an unsigned transfer + Memo transaction using a real Devnet blockhash. Repeated preparation returns the same stored transaction. The client checks the reviewed transaction fields before asking its injected wallet to sign.
5. A successful wallet submission returns a transaction signature. The UI stores that public signature locally for reconciliation and does not automatically submit another transfer after a confirmation error.
6. `POST /api/jobs/:id/solana` with `{action:"confirm",signature}` binds one submitted signature. The server reads Devnet transaction and signature status data and checks success, confirmation, blockhash, payer, recipient, amount, Memo, validity window, allowed instruction programs, absence of inner instructions and balance deltas.
7. A matching receipt is recorded idempotently. `GET /api/jobs/:id/receipt` exports the job evidence, intent and checked receipt, without private keys. Records remain temporary: export before the session expires.

## Evidence

[The captured live receipt](https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/EdgeSwarm/blob/main/docs/evidence/devnet-payment.json) is from an approved disposable-key test through the deployed API. The transfer was confirmed on Devnet and validated server-side. It is not a synthetic transaction. In contrast, negative unit tests deliberately use synthetic RPC fixtures to isolate failure paths. The test harness signed in memory, not through a browser wallet; injected-wallet approval requires an additional browser/wallet integration pass.

The RPC `requestAirdrop` method returned HTTP 410 (closed faucet). The official faucet website funded the test through GitHub authentication. The first in-memory process ended after funding without submitting; a separately approved replacement test completed. No private key was saved to a file or committed. No Mainnet funds or paid services were used.

## Trust model

The backend is a centralized trust domain. It can attest that its own verifier approved its built-in task; the Memo program does not evaluate that policy. The wallet owns the funds and explicitly approves a direct transfer. The chosen recipient is not cryptographically registered as the worker. There is no escrow, refund program, hardware attestation, zk proof, independent verifier operator or on-chain job-level replay lock. A user can send a second payment outside the app; backend idempotence does not prevent that on-chain.

The implementation trusts the public Devnet RPC’s chain view. Confirmed transactions can have weaker finality than finalized transactions. The app is not a production settlement service. Fixed small test amounts reduce demonstration risk, not architectural trust requirements.

## Verification commands

```sh
npm test
npm run build
npm run typecheck
BASE_URL=https://edge-swarm.vercel.app node scripts/smoke.mjs
BASE_URL=https://edge-swarm.vercel.app node scripts/solana-smoke.mjs
```

The first smoke test exercises signed execution, tamper rejection, session isolation and simulated settlement. The second checks actual Devnet genesis/blockhash reads and payment-intent construction, without sending funds. `scripts/devnet-e2e.mjs` is an explicitly gated test-funds harness; never run it without approval. RPC faucet funding may be unavailable; its browser-funding option waits for an approved manual faucet request while retaining keys only in process memory.

## Primary references

- [Solana transaction structure and atomic execution](https://solana.com/docs/core/transactions)
- [Memo program semantics and signer checks](https://www.solana-program.com/docs/memo)
- [Official Devnet faucet](https://faucet.solana.com/)

title: Security and remaining risks
content:
# Security policy and scope

EdgeSwarm is a bounded demonstration, not a production compute/payment network. Report suspected vulnerabilities privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting if enabled; do not publish credentials or live exploit data in issues.

The worker and verifier use separate Ed25519 keys but execute inside the same trusted backend. That is not an independent trust domain, TEE attestation, zk proof, or proof of arbitrary AI correctness. Replay checks only the built-in uppercase transformation.

Anonymous HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies isolate sessions. Writes require a same-origin browser Origin header and JSON object bodies no larger than 64 KiB. Each session allows 100 jobs and 120 API operations per minute. PostgreSQL records become inaccessible after 30 minutes and expired rows are deleted on subsequent requests; the browser cookie is issued for 30 minutes. Cookie rotation bypasses session quotas, so provider-level abuse controls remain necessary.

PostgreSQL holds private demo signing keys. Restrict access, use TLS, separate preview/production databases, and rotate credentials if exposed. Do not expose snapshots through APIs. Runtime APIs never use the legacy Engine file-storage option, which does not persist signing keys and is not a supported restart-safe store.

All job settlement uses simulated credits. `/devnet-demo` is a separate wallet transfer interface, not escrow or verified-work payout. No real transaction was performed for this audit. Android P-256 evidence lacks assignment/nonce/expiry/policy binding and is deliberately ineligible for settlement.

Four moderate npm advisories remain in the Solana web3.js transitive dependency chain at audit time. No high or critical findings were reported by the captured npm audit; this is not a guarantee that the application has no vulnerabilities. Major dependency migrations require compatibility tests, not a blind `npm audit fix --force`.

CSP blocks embedding, objects, and base-URI changes; it is not a strict nonce-based script policy. Authentication, durable financial accounting, independent verifier infrastructure, distributed authorization, complete secret scanning and penetration testing remain outside the verified implementation.

## Verified-job Solana Devnet payments

The new `/api/jobs/:id/solana` API creates a fixed 0.001 test-SOL payment intent only for valid signed job evidence. The payer and recipient are user-selected on-curve wallet addresses and become immutable once prepared. The app constructs a transfer plus a Memo containing job ID, intent ID and evidence digest. It does not custody wallet keys.

Confirmation uses the fixed public Devnet RPC and checks the genesis hash, confirmed/finalized status, transaction success, signature, blockhash, payer signer, exact recipient and amount, memo, balance deltas and unexpected programs/instructions. Transaction evidence is persisted with the temporary session and can be exported. A pasted signature alone is not a receipt.

This is centralized verifier-gated wallet payment, **not on-chain escrow**. The chain executes transfer/Memo instructions, not the job-verification policy. Users can send payments outside the app; no global on-chain double-release protection exists. The recipient is not an authenticated worker. RPC responses are a trust dependency. Public RPC rate limits, session expiry, missing wallet support and insufficient test SOL can block the flow. If signing or confirmation is ambiguous, inspect wallet history and reconcile; do not blindly resend. Synthetic RPC fixtures test validation rules, not real transaction landing.

title: Deployment and PostgreSQL sessions
content:
# Deploy the app separately from the landing page

Keep GitHub Pages as the landing page; its launch links point to the separate live app. Deploy this repository's root Next.js application to Vercel. Pages is a static landing page, not the Jobs API.

## Vercel

1. Import `CodesbyFebin/EdgeSwarm` into your Vercel account, with root directory `.` and framework Next.js. Use Node.js 22 and the lockfile (`npm ci`).
2. Connect a dedicated Neon PostgreSQL database from the Vercel Marketplace. This run created `edgeswarm-postgres` on the Free plan, with Auth and Realtime disabled. Review its limits before increasing usage.
3. Provide the server-only `DATABASE_URL` environment variable (`POSTGRES_URL` is also supported). Never prefix them with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, paste them into chat, or commit them.
4. Deploy. `/api/health` returns 503 on Vercel if storage configuration is missing. It checks configuration, not PostgreSQL connectivity.
5. Run `BASE_URL=https://YOUR-DEPLOYMENT node scripts/smoke.mjs`. If Deployment Protection is enabled, use an approved test path or perform the flows in the authenticated browser. Do not publicly disclose a bypass secret.
6. Manually test `/`, `/mobile`, and `/devnet-demo`. A wallet test requires explicit approval and Devnet-only test SOL. No on-chain test was performed in this audit.
7. Only after the live job/tamper flows pass, add the actual app URL to the Pages landing page. Verified app URL: https://edge-swarm.vercel.app/ (also https://www.agentswarm.in/). Both passed the live API smoke test for commit `785a40b`.

The app fails closed on Vercel without shared storage. It never falls back to filesystem or process memory there. PostgreSQL uses expiring per-session records and revision-checked atomic updates, with retry on conflicts. Tables initialize lazily on first use. Worker/verifier private keys are stored server-side in those records to preserve demo signing identity across instances; protect the database as secret material.

## Local / single-instance Node

Node.js 22 recommended:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm test
npm run build
npm start -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3100
# separate terminal
node scripts/smoke.mjs
```

Without PostgreSQL environment variables, state is disposable process memory. Restarting the server clears jobs and keys. Do not use that fallback with multiple replicas.

A Dockerfile is supplied but was not built during this audit. It is not deployment evidence.

## Operational boundaries

Session cookies isolate anonymous browser demos; they are not user authentication. Jobs and receipts are temporary, and a cleared cookie loses access. Request limits are per session, not per person or IP. Use Vercel's abuse controls and spending limits; cookie rotation can bypass per-session limits. Do not connect real funds, private workloads, or production secrets.

title: Android: what the APK does and does not prove
content:
# Android P-256 evidence interoperability — first integration gate

This adds a Node.js verifier for the **existing** Android local demonstration wire format. It uses the Android-provided X.509 SPKI public key, P-256 ECDSA with SHA-256, DER-encoded signature, and exactly the signed bytes in `MainActivity.kt`. The verifier requires an independently trusted input and an explicit public-key allowlist. It independently recomputes the uppercase output and SHA-256 hashes.

Run `npm test` to execute the Node test suite.

## Security boundary

**LOCAL_DEMO evidence is not settlement eligible.** The Android payload lacks authenticated assignment, coordinator signature, network binding, expiry, nonce, replay ledger, and verifier policy. A self-provided public key is not an identity: the caller must supply registered keys from an authenticated registry. The current JavaScript tests generate a P-256 signature using Node; a real Android-exported JSON fixture and Android instrumentation tests are still required before declaring Kotlin-to-Node interoperability proven.

Next steps: canonical versioned assignment protocol; authenticated Android registration and key rotation; independently deployed verifier; durable evidence/replay state; audited Solana Devnet escrow and finality reconciliation. Never wire this local verifier directly to a payout endpoint.

title: Audit and test evidence
content:
# EdgeSwarm audit and hardening, 2026-11-08

Baseline: `0790837f4d2bc4bbf200f929dddb1803460187f8` on main. This is an engineering review and test pass, not an independent security certification or official hackathon score.

## Final-app and Solana integration follow-up

The user-provided Final EdgeSwarm App archive supplied the visual device shell, brand mark, swipe navigation and tab bar. Its filesystem backend, prepared-payment claims, Mainnet labels, fabricated sample earnings and TypeScript build-error suppression were not carried into the final integration. The screens were connected to the hardened session-scoped backend. Desktop functionality remains at `/dashboard`.

- Final implementation: `9a0febb`, CI [42511366802](https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/EdgeSwarm/actions/runs/42511366802) passed web checks and Android APK build.
- 64 automated tests passed, including adversarial transaction-validation fixtures. Build and TypeScript checks passed.
- Live API smoke and real Devnet RPC intent smoke passed; the latter sends no funds.
- An explicitly approved disposable-wallet test then sent 0.001 Devnet SOL through the live verified-job intent flow. Server-side confirmation, receipt persistence and idempotent confirmation passed. [Explorer](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/37XG6ENuZstcqzfDjcFRR4DnifS1bN12E2id1aAiJ58zTs9246xgonRiA9KmtuHpwmX237MLXkh3y6UhpDP9KqMk?cluster=devnet); [public evidence](https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/EdgeSwarm/blob/main/docs/evidence/devnet-payment.json).
- The first disposable process ended after funding but before transferring; no payment is claimed for it. A separately approved replacement test completed. No private-key files were created.
- Remaining limits: centralized verifier trust; no on-chain escrow/global release guard; no authenticated recipient registration; browser wallet approval and physical Android execution not end-to-end tested; 4 moderate dependency findings remain.

## Evidence

- Baseline: 16 Node tests passed.
- Hardened version: 32 Node tests passed locally, including snapshot/key restoration, tampering after verdict, reward mutation, expiry, duplicate payment, and input validation.
- Next.js 15.5.29 production build and TypeScript check passed during implementation. Final CI is the source of truth for the pushed revision.
- Production API smoke passed after the PostgreSQL refactor locally and live on both `https://edge-swarm.vercel.app` and `https://www.agentswarm.in` for commit `785a40b`; it covers create/process/settle, duplicate settlement, tamper rejection, per-browser isolation, forbidden cross-origin writes, route availability and security headers. Re-run after future deployments.
- Actual hosted Neon PostgreSQL integration passed for separate engine instances, key restoration, concurrent settlement without duplicate payment, session isolation and session expiry configuration.
- Browser desktop flow passed: create job, execute/verify, show `SETTLED`, `HELLO EDGESWARM`, verification PASS, and 50 simulated credits. This is local browser evidence, not live hosting evidence.
- Initial npm audit: six findings (one high, five moderate). PostCSS override and lockfile reduced it to four moderate findings, zero high/critical. Remaining packages: @solana/web3.js, jayson, stream-json, uuid.
- Existing GitHub CI at baseline reported successful web checks and Android APK compilation. That does not establish real-device interoperability. Updated CI run [42506466254](https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/EdgeSwarm/actions/runs/42506466254) passed web tests/build, production API smoke and Android debug APK compilation for `785a40b`.

## Findings and changes

| Finding | Change / remaining limitation |
|---|---|
| Shared unauthenticated state exposed all demo jobs | Per-browser sessions; no claim of real user authentication |
| Serverless instances lose state and signing identities | Shared PostgreSQL records with restored signing keys and atomic compare-and-set updates; Vercel fails closed if unconfigured |
| Unbounded request bodies and job counts | 64 KiB JSON limit, 100 jobs/session, request quota; no IP-wide protection |
| Settlement trusted a status flag and did not re-check changed evidence | Verify signed verdict and re-check result, assignment, nonce, policy, input digest, reward and expiry before simulated payment |
| Reward absent from signed result | Reward now included in signed result and checked before settlement |
| No lockfile / non-reproducible npm install in CI | package-lock.json committed and CI uses npm ci |
| Missing baseline browser security headers | nosniff, frame denial, referrer policy, permissions policy and limited CSP |
| Deployment/README claims inconsistent | Current deployment/security notes take precedence over older design text; Pages landing remains unchanged |
| Restart-unsafe legacy JSON storage | Runtime no longer uses it; unsupported option remains in Engine for historical code compatibility |

## Unfinished requirements

Hosted PostgreSQL connectivity and concurrent settlement were tested. Vercel deployment `J8GwUDtzfA3G4DoCngkFxFD63nsY` is Ready for commit `785a40b`. Live job flows passed on both configured domains. No wallet transaction, production authentication, independent remote verifier, Anchor escrow program, or hardware attestation has been verified. Android code was reviewed but no physical-device test was run. Mobile route exists; a complete mobile accessibility/viewport/device test matrix was not run. Docker was not built. No load test, exhaustive secret-history scan, or penetration test was run.

The supplied MLH submission URL returned Page Not Found. The event deadline and judging rubric therefore remain unverified. There is no defensible official 100/100 score or guaranteed win. A competitive Solana submission still needs a coherent on-chain use case and inspectable transaction evidence; a separate Devnet wallet transfer must not be misrepresented as verified-work settlement.

## Next acceptance criteria

1. Completed: Vercel and free Neon PostgreSQL configured; full live smoke tests passed on both domains.
2. Completed: CI web checks and Android build passed for `785a40b`.
3. Record a short honest demo: valid work settles simulated credits; tampered work does not.
4. Obtain the actual event rubric and decide whether real verified-work Devnet settlement is mandatory before implementing a separate audited program.

title: Three-minute real-app walkthrough

# Three-minute real-app walkthrough

[Play/download the infinitely looping GIF](https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/EdgeSwarm/blob/main/docs/assets/edgeswarm-walkthrough-180s.gif) · [Open the real app](https://edge-swarm.vercel.app/)

The README embeds an optimized GIF made from real browser captures. Encoded duration: **180 seconds**; **180 one-second frames**, **infinite looping**, **1100 × 760 pixels**. Eighteen chapters each occupy ten seconds. A progress bar and elapsed-time counter show the edited walkthrough timeline, not backend execution time.

This is an edited, captioned screenshot walkthrough, not a continuous recording or fabricated interaction animation. No AI-generated app screens were used. Valid and tampered jobs were actually created and processed during capture. The Solana Explorer scenes show the already-approved test transaction, now finalized. No new wallet transfer was sent for this media task.
